source_review.notes: Reviewed eight references for Unix composition, Pipes and Filters, Kahn process networks, software architecture, enterprise messaging, embedded systems, quality attributes, and data-intensive processing. The Unix DOI resolved to ACM, whose automated client returned HTTP 403; the Berkeley book host was temporarily unreachable. These are durable bibliographic and conceptual sources, and the chapter makes no current tool-version claim.

evidence: Reviewed filter, pipe, schema, capacity, order, delivery, service-time, worker-count, rate, backlog, time-interval, identity, and terminal-outcome notation.
Confirmed rate units, nonzero service times, bounded capacities, maximum operation, and functional-composition order are defined before use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Functional semantics, operational capacity, and outcome accounting are kept distinct.

evidence: Recomputed Example 2 capacities as 250, 50, and 166.7 items per second, first-item service as 30 ms, and overload growth as 10 items per second.
Recomputed Example 3 growth as 600 items in 30 seconds, another 400 in 20 seconds to fill 1,000, and recovery from full at 20 items per second as 50 seconds.
Recomputed Exercise 2 capacities as 200, 125, 50, and 100 items per second, bottleneck 50, and 40-second backlog growth as 400 items.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All calculations state fluid, mean-rate, independent-resource, no-loss, and sufficient-capacity assumptions and exclude distributional predictions.

evidence: Verified ideal linear throughput is bounded by every mandatory stage and therefore by the minimum capacity or inverse maximum one-worker service time.
Verified the backlog recurrence adds positive arrival-minus-departure excess and floors negative results at zero before a bounded-capacity policy applies.
Confirmed pure functional composition does not entail scheduling, buffering, durability, latency, or failure properties.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No queueing distribution, exactly-once theorem, or universal scaling law is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed empty input, missing final delimiter, malformed lengths, maximum item size, zero-output filters, multiplicative joins, full queues, hot keys, slow branches, and abrupt closure.

Checked poison items, non-idempotent effects, lost acknowledgments, stale schemas, unit changes, checkpoint crash points, cancellation, sensitive debug taps, compromised sensors, and life-safety overload.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Examples cover pure transformation, capacity, buffering, backpressure, order, effect ambiguity, poison data, schema semantics, cancellation, and clinical safety.

evidence: Traced composition, bottleneck, capacity, acknowledgment, state recovery, ordering, cancellation, security, and evidence invariants through exposition and exercises.
Confirmed stage success, queue delivery, durable acceptance, and externally committed effects are never conflated.
invariant_checking.notes: Every accepted identity must reach a reasoned terminal state under the declared end-to-end contract.

evidence: Reviewed the bottleneck upper-bound argument for a mandatory linear pipeline.
Confirmed every completed item requires service at every mandatory stage, so completion rate cannot exceed any stage capacity.
Confirmed the bound excludes loss, bypass, optional branches, shared-resource interference, and tail-latency conclusions.
proof_review.notes: The proof establishes an ideal upper bound under named item and routing assumptions.

evidence: Audited uses of bound, ideal, stable, complete, durable, exactly once, preserves, correct, safe, proof, and evidence.
Verified fluid backlog, mean service, load tests, fault tests, telemetry, and reconciliation retain explicit scope and limitations.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No local queue, acknowledgment, stage dashboard, or successful run is presented as proof of end-to-end correctness.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter prescribes load, fault, timing, and operational tests but presents no executed code, benchmark, production trace, or reproduced empirical study.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed transformation fit, filter/pipe contracts, historical models, function/operation distinction, framing, cardinality, throughput, latency, buffers, backpressure, ordering, branching, state, time, acknowledgment, effects, retry, cancellation, schema, security, observability, testing, and style boundaries for coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed bounded allocation, overload, queue recovery, worker skew, slow consumers, durable output, effect ambiguity, poison ownership, shutdown, rolling versions, credentials, quarantine retention, high-cardinality telemetry, and failure injection. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified first-principles pipeline vocabulary, derived throughput and backlog models, fifteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in a wildfire-sensor transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
